summary: In ancient Rome, as in Greece, the traditional clan system based on shared bloodlines was replaced by a formal state structure organized around private property and territorial boundaries.
context: Engels demonstrates that the birth of the Roman state followed the universal materialist pattern. Tribal clan democracy was dismantled when private property created class inequalities between rich patricians and poor plebeians.
